title: Security Operations: Monitoring, Triage, Threat Actors and Frameworks

header.html: 5.2 Understand security operations: Logging and monitoring security events; Security event triage (for example incident use cases, prioritization, correlation); Threat actors (for example types, motivations); Cyber threat intelligence; Threat frameworks
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Logging and monitoring

A security operations center (SOC) watches, detects and responds to security events around the clock.

Concept Meaning
Log A record of an event (a login, a file access, a firewall decision)
Event Any observable occurrence
Incident An event (or events) that harms or threatens confidentiality, integrity or availability
SIEM Security information and event management: collects logs from many sources, correlates them and raises alerts
Alert A notification that something needs attention
Good logging practice Why
Log the important sources: firewalls, servers, identity, applications, cloud Visibility
Synchronize clocks (time protocol) Events line up across systems
Protect and retain logs Evidence; attackers delete logs
Review and alert on logs Unread logs do not protect

AI helps SIEM tools by correlating events and reducing alert fatigue; people still decide about real incidents.

Exam tip

. A SIEM collects and correlates; it does not fix. Time synchronization is needed so that logs can be correlated.

2Security event triage

Triage is the quick sorting of alerts to decide what is real, how serious and what to do first.

Step Question
Validate True positive (real attack) or false positive (harmless)?
Prioritize How severe is it, and how critical is the asset?
Correlate Do other events show a pattern (same IP, same user)?
Decide Close, escalate or start incident response
Outcome Meaning
True positive Real threat detected
False positive Alert with no real threat
False negative Real threat missed (the most dangerous)
True negative Normal activity, no alert

Incident use cases are scenarios the SOC prepared for (for example brute force, malware beacon, impossible travel), each with detection rules and a playbook. Routine automated blocks need no action; unusual events need a human.

Exam tip

. Prioritize by severity and asset criticality. A false negative is worse than a false positive.

3Threat actors

Actor Motivation Notes
Nation-state (state-sponsored) Espionage, sabotage, strategic advantage Highly skilled, patient (advanced persistent threat)
Organized crime Money: ransomware, fraud Businesslike
Hacktivist Political or social cause Defacement, leaks, DDoS
Insider Revenge, money or mistake Already has access
Script kiddie Curiosity, fame Low skill, uses tools made by others
Competitor Business advantage Industrial espionage
Exam tip

. Match motive to actor: money = crime, politics = hacktivist, espionage = nation-state, grievance = insider.

4Cyber threat intelligence (CTI)

CTI is evidence-based knowledge about threats that helps decisions.

Level Audience Content
Strategic Executives Trends, who targets the sector
Operational Security managers Campaigns, attacker intent
Tactical Defenders Tactics, techniques, procedures
Technical Tools Indicators of compromise (IoCs): IP addresses, domains, file hashes

Sources include open-source intelligence, vendors, information sharing groups (ISACs) and government.

5Threat frameworks

Framework What it describes
MITRE ATT&CK A catalog of attacker tactics and techniques, based on real observations
Cyber Kill Chain Seven stages of an attack: reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, actions on objectives
Diamond Model Links adversary, capability, infrastructure and victim
STRIDE Threat modeling categories: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege
Exam tip

. ATT&CK = what attackers do (tactics and techniques). Kill Chain = the stages in order. STRIDE = a threat modeling checklist for design.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A system collects logs from firewalls, servers and applications, correlates them and raises alerts. What is it?

  • AA honeypot
  • BA proxy
  • CA VPN
  • DA SIEM
Show the answer

Answer: D. A security information and event management system collects, correlates and alerts.

S2An alert fires for a login from an unusual country, but the employee is on a business trip. What is this alert?

  • AA true negative that needs no further log review
  • BA false positive with no real threat
  • CA false negative that was missed
  • DA true positive for the attack
Show the answer

Answer: B. An alert that turns out to be harmless is a false positive.

S3Which result is the most dangerous for a security team?

  • AA false positive, where a harmless event alerts
  • BA false negative, where a real attack is missed
  • CA true negative, where normal activity is quiet
  • DA true positive, where a real attack is found
Show the answer

Answer: B. A missed real attack gives no chance to respond.

S4A group attacks a government agency for years to steal secrets, with high skill and patience. Which actor fits best?

  • AA script kiddie testing downloaded tools
  • BA hacktivist making a political statement
  • CAn organized crime group seeking money
  • DA nation-state advanced persistent threat
Show the answer

Answer: D. Long, patient, skilled espionage is typical of a nation-state actor.

S5A SOC receives many alerts. Which approach to triage is best?

  • AHandle them in the order they arrive
  • BPrioritize by severity and criticality of the asset
  • CClose all low-count alerts without review
  • DWait until the end of the day for all alerts
Show the answer

Answer: B. Triage prioritizes by severity and by how critical the affected asset is.

S6Which framework is a catalog of attacker tactics and techniques built from real observations?

  • ASTRIDE, a checklist for threat modeling
  • BThe Cyber Kill Chain, a model with seven attack stages
  • CThe Diamond Model, which links four features
  • DMITRE ATT&CK, a matrix of tactics and techniques
Show the answer

Answer: D. MITRE ATT&CK catalogs attacker tactics and techniques seen in real attacks.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does a SIEM do?

Show the answer

Collects logs, correlates events and raises alerts.

R2What is a false positive?

Show the answer

An alert with no real threat.

R3Which actor is motivated by political causes?

Show the answer

A hacktivist.

R4What are indicators of compromise?

Show the answer

Evidence such as IP addresses, domains and file hashes.

R5How many stages does the Cyber Kill Chain have?

Show the answer

Seven.

R6What does the S in STRIDE stand for?

Show the answer

Spoofing.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Logging SIEM collects and correlates; synchronize clocks; protect logs
Triage validate, prioritize, correlate, decide; false negative is worst
Actors nation-state, organized crime, hacktivist, insider, script kiddie
CTI strategic, operational, tactical, technical (IoCs)
Frameworks ATT&CK, Kill Chain (7 stages), Diamond Model, STRIDE
